findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with a biofilm. The PIC was informed and turned off the machine. The facility will purchase food-grade ice for service until the machine can be emptied and sanitized. Inspector will follow-up on July 31, 2026 to ensure the ice machine interior is clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the floor and walls below the triple sink and dish machine to be damaged and harboring drain flies. The PIC stated that a previous inspector advised sealing the wall with spray foam, but this foam is not easily cleanable and therefore has become damaged and soiled over time. Inspector recommends cutting out all foam and repairing with a durable, non-absorbent material (painted drywall, NUDO panel, silicone sealant, etc.). Removing this foam will also benefit in pest control measures. Ensure walls and floors are sealed to be smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee transfer fully prepared garlic bread and bread sticks from the oven to a plate for customer service with their bare hands. The employee was educated when the action was observed and the bread was immediately discarded. The employee proceeded to put on gloves to prepare food. The PIC will be further educating employees about proper handling of ready-to-eat foods. Ensure that employee always use a barrier (ex. gloves, deli tissue, utensils) to handle all ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed cinnamon sugar was being stored in a heavily soiled plastic container. During the inspection the cinnamon sugar was moved into a new container and the old soiled container was discarded. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following require cleaning: 

(1) The dust on the wire shelves holding clean dishes by the main kitchen entrance door.

(2) The debris on the bottom of the container holding clean utensils on the shelf underneath the left warmer. 

(3) The debris on the surface against the coffee pot top at the bar and gaming room. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation or dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed 3 instances of a #16 violation.

-The first instance observed was the can opener blade. Inspector observed the blade to be soiled with food residue. CORRECTED discussed with PIC and PIC had the blade removed from the assembly. Ensure the blade of the can opener is cleaned regularly enough to keep it clean.

-The second instance was a stock pot with pasta dried to the inside. Ensure that all dishes are washed appropriately after each use. Dishes must be clean to sight and touch. CORRECTED PIC had the pot washed, rinsed, and sanitized.

-The third instance was the ice machine baffle. Inspector observed there to be a build-up of soils on the ice machine baffle. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the baffle is cleaned regularly enough to prevent the build-up of soils.

Inspector will return 08/04/2025 to re-inspect the baffle.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the facility to be using steam tables to reheat food. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that all food is brought up to 165 for 15 seconds before going in to hot-holding. Inspector will return 08/04/2025 to re-inspect reheating procedures.
findings.citation_text: 3-403.11(A) Reheating for Hot Holding. (A) Except as specified under (B) and (C) and in (E) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the FOOD reach a temperature of at least 74°C (165°F) for 15 seconds.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the can opener blade to be soiled with food debris. Discussed the soiled can opener with PIC. PIC cleaned the entire can opener insert immediately. Ensure the can opener is cleaned regularly enough to keep the blade free of food debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the underside of the soda machine to contain food residue and soils. The specific area is the underside of the dispensers, next to the soda nozzles. The soda nozzles were clean. Discussed the soiled underside of the machine with the PIC. Ensure the machine is cleaned regularly enough to prevent the build up of food residue and soils.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the prep counter next to the back door to be cracked and showing particle board underneath the veneer. Discussed the cracking with PIC. Ensure that the surface is caulked, refinished, or replaced to allow for a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

Inspector observed bare wood on the wall behind the basket fryers on the cook line. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that this wood is painted or sealed to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: Inspector observed personal drinks stored in areas where clean utensils and or food for sale to the public is located. Ensure that personal drinks are stored properly and only kept in containers with lids and straws. Hand washing after taking a break from the task to drink is also important.
 (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Inspector observed the dish machine to have 0ppm of available chlorine when tested. The container of chlorine appeared off color (more white or clear). The bucket was changed and the dish machine primed. It is now testing out at 50ppm of chlorine. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: Inspector observed a container of Alfredo in the 3 door cooler at 60F internally. The container had been filled to over 4 inches and the lid was tight on the container. A portion of the Alfredo had already been utilized. The sauce was made today and had proper date marking on it. The sauce had another half hour to come down to 40F. The remainder of the sauce was placed into an ice bath to help ensure that it met the cooling benchmark. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: Inspector observed that employees are using cloth towels with spray bottles of sanitizer. Discontinue this practice. Ensure that spray bottles are used with disposable/single use paper towels OR cloth towels are used with buckets of sanitizer and properly stored in the sanitizer between uses. 

(A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11:  Inspector observed that the seals on several pieces of cold holding equipment are in disrepair. Both make table reach in sections, the glass front holding pasta near the cook line and the glass front holding dressing at the server station all have seals which are torn or broken/no longer intact. These seals leak air and are not longer cleanable. Repair these pieces of equipment and maintain them in good repair.

(A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: Inspector observed areas behind the dish machine and 3 part sink are sealed with foam sealant. Also, the area under the pizza ovens is sealed with foam sealant. Cut down foam in these areas so that it is smooth and seal foam so that the areas are non absorbent and easily cleanable. 

(A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Ice machine baffle was observed to contain an accumulation of mold.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on-site.  Ensure ice machine is cleaned regularly, inspector suggested adding this task to cleaning schedule.

4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Multiple containers of dressings made in-house were observed to not be date marked. Discussed with PIC, corrected on-site.  Ensure all dressing containers and to go containers are date marked and discarded 7 days after they are made.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Several cockroaches were observed in the mop and dish areas.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure pest control is contacted to treat as soon as possible.  In the meantime, clean back area (kitchen, dish, mop areas) and seal gaps and holes to help prevent pest harborage.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
There are still multiple areas throughout the kitchen that need the coving secured to the wall.  Discussed with PIC, this is a violation not corrected from the pre-opening inspection.  Ensure all the coving is sealed to the wall to create a smooth, easily cleanable surface and to prevent pest harborage.

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
There are multiple areas throughout the kitchen in need of caulking/sealing:
1.  Edging piece between soda room and kitchen (from pre-opening)
2.  Edging and coving in same area, cease use of foil currently there (from pre-opening)
3.  Holes in the walls throughout the kitchen
4.  Stainless steel covering behind the fryers needs to be re-attached
5.  Other doorways and corners are throughout the kitchen that need to be sealed
Ensure all areas are sealed/caulked to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface and to also prevent pest harborage.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Cleaning throughout the kitchen under equipment and shelving is necessary.  Discussed with PIC, advised adjusting staff cleaning schedule to ensure all along the wall and floor junctures are scraped, scrubbed, and cleaned.  This will also help prevent pest/rodent harborage.  Ensure equipment is pulled out and cleaned underneath/behind.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
